article: LoadIconはDestroyIconを呼び出す必要はない
scope: Read the complete Japanese source and all twelve translations. Compared ownership and cleanup guidance for LoadIcon, LoadImage with and without LR_SHARED, CopyImage with LR_COPYRETURNORG, CopyIcon, CreateIconIndirect, and CreateIconFromResource APIs with Microsoft Learn.
findings: Clarified that LoadIcon handles are shared and must not be passed to DestroyIcon; added the corresponding LoadImage LR_SHARED rule and the caller-owned LR_SHARED-absent rule.
Added CopyImage LR_COPYRETURNORG and CopyIcon ownership details from their function-specific documentation.

Found contradictory Microsoft documentation: the DestroyIcon overview lists CreateIconFromResource among shared-icon sources, while the individual CreateIconFromResource page says to call DestroyIcon; the Ex page also conflicts with LR_SHARED semantics. The article explicitly flags this rather than giving a false universal rule.
Replaced the single DestroyIcon citation with seven direct Microsoft Learn references in all editions.
Removed duplicate date metadata in all editions, retained the 2024-04-19 publication date, and set lastmod to 2026-11-24.

post/LoadIconはDestroyIconを呼び出す必要はない/inde.summary: Compared all localized guidance with current Microsoft Learn pages for DestroyIcon, LoadIcon, LoadImage, CopyIcon, CopyImage, and CreateIconFromResource APIs. Clarified shared versus caller-owned icon handles and explicitly noted conflicting ownership instructions in the CreateIconFromResource documentation.

meaning.note: All editions distinguish shared LoadIcon/LR_SHARED handles from caller-owned icons and preserve the same caveat about contradictory CreateIconFromResource documentation.

terminology.note: Icon handle ownership, shared resources, caller-owned resources, DestroyIcon, LR_SHARED, and LR_COPYRETURNORG remain distinct across translations.

mathematics.note: The article contains no mathematical claims or formulas.

code.note: The article contains API names and flags but no executable code sample.

links.note: All seven Microsoft Learn references match across editions and support the ownership statements, including the documented inconsistency.

limitations: AI-assisted review; no human or native-speaker certification.
Microsoft Learn pages conflict on CreateIconFromResource and CreateIconFromResourceEx ownership guidance; the article flags this and does not assert a universal rule for those APIs.
